newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Yanjing Beer plans May issue of A shares.
newsitem.headline: China's Yanjing Beer plans May issue of A shares.

text.p: China's biggest brewer Yanjing Beer Group Co is planning to raise 560 million yuan ($67 million) by issuing domestic currency A shares to be listed in Shenzhen, company officials and state media said on Wednesday.

The brewer would inject assets worth 310 million yuan into the Yanjing Beer Shareholding Co, which would make a public issue of 80 million shares priced at 7.14-7.16 yuan each, the Beijing Economic Daily said.
A company official said the shares would be listed in May in Shenzhen, with the main underwriter Beijing Securities Co.
The money raised from the share issue would be used to carry out technical improvements, the Beijing Economic Daily said.
Yanjing was also preparating for listing in Hong Kong under a joint project with the Beijing government, the newspaper said.
The brewer, which controls 85 percent of the Beijing beer market, had achieved average profits of 0.49 yuan per share over the last three years, the official said.

Yanjing brewed 571,000 tonnes of beer last year, up 68.2 percent from 1995, making it China's largest brewery, the Beijing Economic Daily said in January. Pre-tax profits last year soared 58.2 percent from 1995 to 357.99 million yuan.
